papers.title_in_file: Equivalence between exponential concentration in quantum machine learning kernels and barren plateaus in variational algorithms
papers.what_it_is: Proves a construction mapping a parametrized quantum neural network to a quantum kernel that inherits its concentration properties.

assertions.value: The paper proves that, under its construction, a QNN with a BP landscape or a BP-free landscape has a corresponding quantum kernel to which the variance bounds transfer.
quotes: Theorem 1. Given a QNN as defined in Eq. (4) that follows either an asymptotic exponential upper bound (BP landscape) or polynomial lower bound (BP-free landscape), there exists a quantum kernel as defined by Eq. (9) such that the variance bounds transfer to the quantum kernel variance.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 1 with proof in Appendix A.

assertions.value: The authors state that constructing a quantum kernel from a BP-free QNN does not guarantee that the kernel is practically useful or has an advantage over classical kernels.
quotes: does not guarantee that the resulting quantum kernel is practically useful or has an advantage over classical kernels.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own stated limit of the result.

assertions.value: The authors state that the results imply a QNN with a BP leads to quantum kernels that suffer from EC, whereas a BP-free QNN can be used to build a quantum kernel that does not exhibit exponential concentration.
quotes: Our results imply that a QNN with a BP leads to quantum kernels that suffer from EC, whereas, more importantly, a BP-free QNN can be used to build a quantum kernel that does not exhibit exponential concentration.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated implication in the conclusion; the proved part is Theorem 1.
